name: Waldorf Astoria Seychelles Platte Island
positioning: Private-island villa resort on Platte Island in the Seychelles Outer Islands, reached only by private plane
best_for: Couples wanting a villa with a private pool and direct beach access
Nature lovers interested in turtle conservation and snorkeling
Families with children who enjoy nature and marine activities

facts.text: Platte Island lies in the Indian Ocean, around 130 kilometers south of Mahé, and is part of the Seychelles Outer Islands.
Platte Island is a sand cay that was originally an uninhabited coconut plantation.
Before the flight, an airport concierge escorts guests to the Waldorf Astoria Lounge above the domestic terminal check-in, with WiFi, complimentary drinks and showers.
La Perle offers poolside dining inspired by Northern Mediterranean and Asian cuisines.
Maison Des Epices serves Creole and Latino cooking, with open-fire cooking and handmade spices.
Lalin is a bar with ocean views, an extensive liquor collection and cocktails from sunset.
Torti serves light lunches, cool drinks and Asian cuisine.
The Waldorf Astoria Spa has six treatment suites.
The spa has a hamam, a hydro pool, an infinity pool and a sauna with Himalayan pink salt walls.
Activities include snorkeling, diving, guided sunrise wildlife walks, sunset yoga and masterclasses.
The Sea Scouts Kids Club offers nature-based activities, arts and crafts, and cooking classes.
The island is about 95 percent solar-powered.

highlights.text: All villa buildings are set back from the beach so hawksbill turtles can keep laying their eggs undisturbed.
The resident environmental manager runs a turtle conservation program and takes guests on early-morning patrols to find and document new nests.
Villas have a large terrace, a private pool and direct beach access from the villa's own garden.
Champagne Rock is the island's natural beach bar, and floating breakfasts can be served in the villa's private pool.
Moulin uses seasonal produce harvested from the restaurant's own garden.

considerations.text: The island is reached only by private plane, and the flight is charged for a fee.
Paths are sandy, which might make wheelchair use hard.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the resort's ultra-luxury positioning.
